report.title: Reconstruct the exact bypass used in real malicious-extension and package incidents
report.question: For a set of documented malicious extension and package incidents, what was the EXACT mechanism that got past review (obfuscated payload, post-install script, update-after-approval, dependency confusion) - and which of those mechanisms is possible against a prompt-payload marketplace?

incident_table.title: npm event-stream 3.3.6 / flatmap-stream after maintainer transfer
incident_table.exact_mechanism: After publishing rights for event-stream moved to a new maintainer, event-stream@3.3.6 added a new dependency flatmap-stream. npm Security's postmortem states the injected code read AES-encrypted data from a file disguised as a test fixture and targeted Copay builds. The malicious dependency was later replaced on the registry by a security-holding package.
incident_table.evidence_grade_notes: OSV GHSA-mh6f-8j2x-4483 (API) plus the npm Security blog (prose) independently record that event-stream@3.3.6 gained the malicious flatmap-stream dependency. The AES-encrypted-fixture technique is named by two prose sources (npm blog and LWN) and is therefore E3 under the unit's API+prose rule, not a measured fact.

needles: AES encrypted data from a file disguised as a test fixture

incident_table.applicability_reason: A later version of an already-trusted package_id is installed when marketplace_install is invoked with a new package_version whose digest and signature pass. tools/marketplace/verify.py has no human-review gate; tools/plugin/installer.py activates a new transaction_id and atomically retargets plugins/<id>. That is the same 'update after the first review' shape as event-stream@3.3.6. Obfuscation of SKILL.md / hook JSON is separately applicable as a review-evasion property of text payloads; the AES-fixture recipe itself is E3.

incident_table.title: npm ua-parser-js 0.7.29 / 0.8.0 / 1.0.0 after account hijack
incident_table.exact_mechanism: Three versions of ua-parser-js (0.7.29, 0.8.0, 1.0.0) were published with embedded malware after the npm account was hijacked. OSV GHSA-pjwm-rvh2-c87w and CISA name those versions. Sonatype's write-up (E3 for the exact script names) reports identical preinstall and postinstall Bash/Batch scripts. The malicious versions are absent from the live versions object on registry.npmjs.org while their timestamps remain in the time map.
incident_table.evidence_grade_notes: OSV (API) and CISA (prose) both name versions 0.7.29, 0.8.0, and 1.0.0 as malicious. The preinstall/postinstall script detail is presently one prose rail (Sonatype) so it is E3. Applicability of the post-install-script *class* does not depend on that E3 detail: this tree never runs package scripts.
incident_table.applicability_reason: npm lifecycle scripts fire because the package manager executes scripts.postinstall during install. tools/plugin/installer.py extracts a tar with filter='data' and shutil.copy2 of the projection map; it does not import subprocess or call os.system. tools/marketplace/install.py never extracts. A planted package.json postinstall in the tarball is at most a copied file.

incident_table.title: PyPI torchtriton vs PyTorch extra-index dependency confusion
incident_table.exact_mechanism: A package named torchtriton was registered on the public PyPI index with the same name as a dependency normally fetched from the PyTorch nightly extra index. The PyTorch postmortem states that because the PyPI index takes precedence (pip#8606), pip installed the PyPI package instead of the official nightly artifact. The name remains reserved on PyPI simple (HTTP 200, no files).
incident_table.evidence_grade_notes: PyPI simple (API) shows the torchtriton project is registered. The PyTorch blog (prose) states the holiday-window compromise and that the PyPI index takes precedence.
incident_table.applicability_reason: tools/marketplace/fetch.py _read_source accepts only an existing local file or a file: URL and raises FetchError for any other source. There is no package-name resolver and no extra-index-url. verify.check_lockfile_digest pins sha256. Classic name-collision across indexes cannot occur on this install path.

incident_table.title: Chrome Web Store The Great Suspender ownership transfer then malicious update
incident_table.exact_mechanism: The original maintainer announced a change of administration (GitHub issue 1175). Issue 1263 records that the extension was sold, that v7.1.8 published to the web store (not GitHub) loaded remote obfuscated code, and that a later store update can ship without notifying the user. This row is prose+prose (E3) and is not cited as a measured fact; update-after-approval is measured via INC-EVENT-STREAM-2018.
incident_table.evidence_grade_notes: GitHub issues 1175 and 1263 are both prose. Wayback CDX is an API rail but does not attest the sale or v7.1.8 payload. Graded E3. Included because it is the closest extension-marketplace analogue; it does not carry any measured claim by itself.

needles: arbitrary code was executed from a remote server

incident_table.applicability_reason: Same install-path fact as event-stream: a new signed, digest-matching version of package_id replaces the live symlink with no review gate in run_verification. E3 for the Chrome-store narrative; the local applicability argument does not depend on that E3 row because INC-EVENT-STREAM-2018 already measures the class.

mechanism_map.reason: SKILL.md and hooks/pre.json are reviewable text. Encoded or comment-hidden instructions can sit in those files after a human review of the 'obvious' markdown. bin/demo is an executable shim whose bits are preserved (0755) but not run at install. The event-stream AES-fixture recipe is E3; the review-evasion property of opaque text in this payload type is still applicable.
Installer and marketplace never execute package lifecycle scripts. See INC-UA-PARSER-JS-2021 applicability_reason.
New package_version of the same package_id is a new transaction activation. Digest+signature are checked; human review is not.
Fetch is explicit file/file: URL plus sha256 lockfile pin. No name-based multi-index resolver exists on this path.

payload_types.note: Mode 0755 is preserved on extract/copy. The installer does not execute the shim.

mitigations.claim: A blob whose sha256 does not match lockfile.packages[ref].digest fails closed and never reaches the plugin installer.
Missing or non-ed25519 signatures raise GateFailure; unsigned packages are not installed.
Plugin install extracts and copies projected files. It does not run npm/pip lifecycle scripts.

extensions.notes: G-1 delivery of RES-0055. Claims graded E3 are labelled and are not cited as measured fact. Did not run global unit_manifest.py --write. cloud ok=true is not delivery. No exploit against a third-party system was executed.
